# Modem 2.0: The Customer Product Graph

Ben Vinegar

• November 18, 2026• 7 min read

Modem 2.0 is out today. It connects what your customers are saying about your product to the tickets and code changes your team ships, and it works from Claude Code, ChatGPT, Cursor or whatever agent you already use.

We messed up.

Back in March we launched Modem as an AI product manager. It was an agent that listened to your customer conversations and stayed on top of your tasks. You could ask it who wanted webhooks, or tell it to file the ticket, and it did.

On paper it was a pretty solid idea. PMs were some of the most sought after and expensive people in tech, and agents had already taken on a good chunk of coding. Why not product management too?

...

Customers described Modem differently anyways. What drove value for them wasn't the agent, but the data Modem collects and aggregates: customer concerns aggregated from your channels, connected to the tickets and pull requests that close the work.

So we took the most valuable part of what we'd built - the graph powering our agent's brain - and made it available to every agent. We call it the customer product graph.

- Cursor
- ChatGPT
- Claude Code

Your customer channels go in one side. The agent you already use reads from the other.

## The customer product graph

Modem monitors your group chat, support tickets and sales calls. When three customers complain about checkout failing – one in chat, one in a support ticket, one on a call – Modem groups them into one topic.

A topic is one customer problem with every report of it attached. If more customers bring it up next week, those reports get filed under the same topic.

Here's what one looks like in Modem:

One topic and everything it is linked to, in Modem.

- Problem statement. Modem distills scattered conversations into a summary you can actually read.
- Status. Is this concern being worked on? Is it already fixed? Modem updates the status as tickets op
